lead: Joins related buttons into one. The theme style handles the corners, seams and dividers; `variant` / `color` / `size` / `radius` / `disabled` on the group reach the buttons in it through context, as their defaults. The examples follow the ButtonGroup page of the HeroUI docs.

anatomy.title: Anatomy
anatomy.description: ButtonGroup wraps a few Buttons; the optional ButtonGroup.Separator goes inside a button.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: How HeroUI's primary / secondary / tertiary / outline / ghost / danger are written in this package; the mapping is on the [Button](/button) page.

disabled-state.title: Disabled State
disabled-state.override: Group disabled, but one button overrides

without-separator.title: Without Separator
without-separator.description: Leave out ButtonGroup.Separator and there is no divider.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: HeroUI v3 has no `color`. This is the `variant` × `color` matrix of this package, to check the seams of every theme style.

radius.title: Radius
radius.description: Only the two ends keep their outer corners rounded; the seams are square.

overrides.title: Overrides
overrides.description: A button's own `variant` / `color` win over the group's; a `loading` button ignores clicks inside a group too.

api.title: API Reference
api.separator: Takes the native attributes of a `span`. Put it inside a button (usually as the first child) to draw a divider at the seam with the previous button; leave it out for no divider. Variants with a border rely on the overlapping borders, so the theme style hides it there.

styling.title: Styling Reference
styling.description: Like Button, the component has no styles and only writes hooks; theme styles handle the seams in `button-group.css`.
styling.orientation: Group direction: theme styles use it to pick which corners merge at the seams and which way the dividers run
styling.variants: Only present when the matching prop is passed; the same values reach the buttons in the group through context
styling.position: Buttons in a group carry no position attribute: merging the corners at the seams relies on structural pseudo-classes only, so the group's direct children must be buttons
